title: Linkability of User Activities Over Time
description: GPS traces and timestamps in sensor batches allow linking user activities across different sessions, enabling tracking of movement patterns and behavior over time.
assumptions: Data is transmitted without anonymization or aggregation.

title: Direct Identification via Device ID
description: Transmission of unique device ID enables direct identification of the user, potentially linking data to a specific individual.
assumptions: Device ID is unique and not pseudonymized.

title: Eavesdropping on Data in Transit
description: Unencrypted transmission of sensor data between wearable and app could allow interception of sensitive information like GPS traces.

title: Insecure Data Storage at Destination
description: Companion app may store synced sensor data without adequate security controls, risking unauthorized access.
assumptions: App stores data locally or in cloud without encryption/access controls.

title: Lack of User Awareness About Data Collection
description: Users may not be informed that their sensor data (e.g., GPS, exercise sessions) is being synced to the app.
assumptions: Privacy policy or consent mechanisms are unclear or absent.

title: Non-Compliance with Data Protection Laws
description: App's handling of synced data may violate regulations (e.g., GDPR) if data is processed without legal basis or user consent.
assumptions: App lacks compliance measures for data processing activities.
